title: Regional ambassador fallback and evacuation playbook
content:
Summary:

This is a working playbook describing a lightweight "ambassador" per-region control-plane façade and an explicit evacuation/fallback procedure for regional control-plane degradation. Goal: keep serving stable while minimizing risk of split-brain, and provide clear operator steps to move control responsibilities between regions with minimal disruption to routing and SLOs.

Motivation / problem statement:
- We operate in multiple cloud regions with independent control-plane cells. We need a pattern that:
  * lets local region services read local control state quickly,
  * enables fast failover to another region when a control-cell becomes unhealthy, and
  * avoids dangerous split-brain/write conflicts during partition and recovery.
- Existing ideas (active-active full mesh, active-passive master/standby) each have tradeoffs around latency, cost, complexity of state sync, and risk of conflicting writes. This doc proposes a hybrid operational model leveraging regional ambassadors plus an evacuation protocol.

Key concepts (short):
- Ambassador: a small, highly-available proxy layer running in each region. Exposes the same control-plane API surface but can route to local control cell or remote leader(s). Bearer-token and region affinity enforced.
- Local leader lease: a short TTL lease that authorizes a region to accept writes for given tenant partitions. Leases require either a majority of arbiters (preferred) or an external arbiter service to validate.
- Evacuation: orchestrated handoff when health signals cross thresholds. Evacuation can be local->remote or remote->local recovery.
- Read-only shadow mode: during removal/hand-off, a region can enter read-only to drain writes and serve reads until a handoff is complete.

High-level topology options compared (operator-friendly):
1) Active-passive (leader + standby):
   - Write path always goes to leader region, reads can be served by ambassadors locally (with eventual read-after-write caveat).
   - Pros: simple conflict model, easy to reason about consistency.
   - Cons: increased latency for some tenants; standby must keep state sync up-to-date (sync window complexity).
2) Active-active selective partitioning:
   - Owners partition tenant keyspaces, each region leads for subsets of tenants. Cross-region writes limited to global coordination.
   - Pros: latency-optimized, scales write capacity.
   - Cons: complex shard assignments and handoff; risk of inconsistent writes on failure.
3) Ambassador-hybrid (ours):
   - Ambassadors route writes to elected leader(s) using leases. Ambassadors implement evacuation runbook hooks and can force read-only when handoff is underway.
   - Pros: operationally flexible, controlled evacuation, safer than naive active-active; lower tail latency for reads.
   - Cons: added proxy layer and orchestration complexity.

Leader election and lease model (recommended):
- Use short TTL leases (15s–60s depending on heartbeat reliability) stored in a durable backing (multi-region KV or arbiter quorum).
- Election triggers: sustained health failure of local control cell, majority of arbiters reporting unreachable, or manual operator command.
- Fencing token: when a new leader is granted a lease, it receives a fencing token (monotonic counter) used to reject late writes from previous leader. Ambassadors include token with write requests.
- Arbiter recommendation: run a lightweight arbiter fleet (odd number) in separate zones/regions to reduce split-brain risk without requiring full quorum across all control cells.

Evacuation runbook (operator steps, checklist style):
1) Detect: health probes crossing thresholds: control-plane reconcile latency > X ms for > Y minutes, KV write errors > 0.5% for 5m.
2) Preflight: ambassadors switch write routing to prefer local cell but allow fallback; mark region as "degraded" in routing metadata.
3) Drain writes: flip local control cells to read-only mode (graceful), allowing in-flight requests to complete.
4) Acquire remote lease: target region operator initiates lease acquisition via arbiter workflow. Confirm fencing token handshake.
5) Reroute ambassadors: ambassador config pushes to route writes to new leader; read affinity preserved where possible.
6) Validate: smoke tests, end-to-end eval, check data lag metrics (sync_delay < acceptable window) and token acceptance.
7) Promote: finalize promotion, update global routing catalogs, remove read-only guard on new leader.
8) Post-mortem: capture root cause, timing of state transitions, and any anomalies.

Ambassador behaviour details:
- Health weighting: ambassadors combine control-plane health (local cell) + infra signals (instance CPU, network RTT) to compute regional weight.
- Circuit breaker: if local control cell errors exceed threshold, ambassador stops routing writes locally and either forwards to remote or returns structured 503 with hint (Retry-After + next-leader).
- Cache and KV shadow reads: for reducing latency, ambassadors can serve strongly-cached config reads for short TTLs; must not serve stale object writes during evacuations.
- Observability hooks: ambassadors emit routing decisions, lease tokens used per request, and handoff events to the tracing system.

Safety knobs and metrics to monitor:
- metrics: lease_acquire_latency, lease_renew_failures, ambassador_forward_rate, write_retries, fencing_rejections, synced_lag_seconds, region_evacuations_count
- SLOs: <= 1% increase in p99 latency during planned handoffs; failures during evacuation must be < 0.1% of writes.
- Safety knobs: forced read-only global flag, ambassador-level rate-limiters, and an emergency manual fence to invalidate old leases.

Edge cases and gotchas:
- Network partition where arbiter -> control cells isolated: prefer manual intervention and conservative read-only gating to avoid split brain.
- Slow state sync can cause long read-after-write inconsistencies even if routing succeeded — enforce per-tenant acceptable lag and limit cross-region write rates for those tenants.
- Clock skew effects: use monotonic counters + fencing tokens, avoid relying on wall-clock timestamps for leader validity.

Operational playbook snippets (quick):
- To force evacuation from region-a to region-b: set region-a ambassadors to "degraded" mode, promote region-b lease with fencing token, push ambassador route changes, run smoke, flip GLOABL route catalog.
- To roll back: put new leader into read-only immediately, instruct ambassadors to retry old leader after manual validation, ensure fencing tokens are revoked and replaced.

Open questions / decisions required:
- Arbiter placement: how many and where? (recommend odd 3 with at least 2 in primary clouds)
- Lease TTL tuning depending on user traffic patterns (we need a small test matrix).
- Automation level for evacuation (semi-automated vs fully automated based on severity thresholds).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is an operational-first proposal; engineering teams should iterate on ambassador implementation and the arbiter mechanism in the next sprint.
- I want feedback on acceptable sync lag for the top 10 tenants and whether we should restrict cross-region writes during handoffs by default.

Appendix: Command snippets and links
- Quick verification: curl ambassador.region-a.internal/healthz -> returns {status:degraded, lease:ex123, leader:region-b}
- Smoke tests: github link in linked_artifacts above for sample scripts.

(End of draft)
